title: Org invite governance - RBAC v2 scoping, email allowlist automation, and SAML domain reconciliation
creator: Marcus Li
description: Goal: Implement a unified invite governance flow that ties RBAC v2 role scoping to organizational invite policies, automates email allowlist/denylist enforcement at invite time, and reconciles SAML/IdP domain assertions with domain verification/audit logs. This ticket covers backend rule evaluation, audit-log enrichment, migration path for existing orgs, and a small admin UI surface to surface policy mismatches and reconciliation results. Success metrics: zero new SSO bypass incidents in staging; >=95% reduction in manual domain attach requests for customers on enforced allowlists; audit logs show policy-evaluation reason for every allow/deny decision.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Invite processing pipeline evaluates RBAC v2 role constraints and invite policies atomically and writes a single normalized audit entry for each invite (who, inviter, target email, policy snapshot, decision, reason). 2) Email allowlist/denylist rules support exact domain match, wildcard, and regex patterns and are enforced pre-invite submission to avoid race windows. 3) SAML assertion domains are automatically reconciled with org-verified domains (reconciliation job reports mismatches). 4) Migration job safely transitions orgs using legacy invite rules to the new engine with an opt-in dry-run mode. 5) Admin UI surfaces a policy simulator and reconciliation report. 6) E2E tests cover happy/failure paths and observability dashboards for invite-failure rates.
scope: In scope: invite-time rule evaluation service, audit log format changes, allowlist rule engine, SAML domain reconciliation job, small admin console pages (reconciliation report + simulator), migration/dry-run path, e2e and load tests. Out of scope: full RBAC v2 role editor UX and enterprise policy admin delegation flows (these are separate tickets).
approach: 1) Add a new Invite Policy Evaluator microservice (stateless) that accepts invite requests and returns a decision plus rationale. 2) Integrate the evaluator into API gateway path used by console and API invite endpoints. 3) Extend audit log schema to include policy_snapshot_id, evaluation_reason, and used_saml_claims. 4) Implement reconciliation batch job that consumes SAML assertion logs and compares claimed domains with verified domains, writing reconciliation findings to a new admin report S3 key. 5) Build a console report UI that reads reconciliation findings and shows suggested next steps (mark domain verified, contact user, or block). 6) Migration: run evaluator in dry-run for 2 weeks, compare outcomes vs legacy behavior, report discrepancies, then flip to enforce for orgs that opt-in and finally roll out globally with rollback plan.
tradeoffs: - Centralized evaluator increases runtime dependency but simplifies reasoning and ensures consistent logs; mitigated via cold-standby and caching. - Strict pre-invite enforcement prevents some edge-case invites (e.g., transient corporate aliases) but reduces security incidents; we will provide a temporary manual override for org admins for specific emails while reconciliation completes. - Regex allowlist support is powerful but can be slow and error-prone; regex entries will be evaluated after exact/wildcard matches and rate-limited in admin UI to avoid DoS via complex patterns.
migration_plan: Phase 0: schema change for audit log (backwards compatible). Phase 1: deploy evaluator in dry-run mode for a subset of orgs (internal + canary customers). Phase 2: surface discrepancies to org admins via console report and collect feedback. Phase 3: opt-in enforcement for customers with verified domains. Phase 4: global enforcement with automated rollback triggers (spike in support tickets, invite failure rate > 0.2%).
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for evaluator rule combinatorics, integration tests for API path, load test to 5k invites/min to validate latency SLO (95th < 150ms), reconciliation job test harness with synthetic SAML logs, E2E with console simulator. Add alerts on invite-failure spikes and reconciliation job errors.
monitoring: Dashboards: invites-by-decision, invites-by-reason, reconciliation-mismatch-counts, invites-latency-p95. Alerts: reconciliation job failure, invite-failure-rate > 0.2% for > 10 minutes, audit-log write errors. Create a LogQL query for quick investigation and a prebuilt Grafana panel linked in the PR description.
rollout_and_rollback: Canary to 10% of orgs (internal first) with dry-run comparisons visible. Roll forward if invite-failure delta < 0.05% and no high-severity support tickets. Rollback path: disable evaluator hook at gateway and revert audit log schema change via feature flag.
implementation_notes: - Audit log format change will use a new JSON field 'invite_policy' and write to the same event stream to keep downstream consumers compatible. - Use existing SAML claim extractor library to avoid re-parsing. - Store allowlist rules in config service with versioned snapshots; evaluator takes a snapshot id for deterministic audits. - For RBAC v2 constraints, convert role scoping directives into a canonical constraint language before evaluation.

2026-03-09: Load tests completed in staging: 5k invites/min sustained, p95 110ms; reconciliation job runs in <8s per 10k SAML events.

notes_for_pm: PM should coordinate customer opt-in communication and support playbook. Provide list of initial canary orgs and acceptance criteria for opt-in. Ensure legal/compliance sign-off for audit log retention changes.
final_notes: This ticket aims to reduce operational friction (manual domain attachments, support tickets) while tightening invite-time security. Keep the dry-run window long enough to capture enterprise provisioning patterns (recommended 14 days).
